```{r citation-data, include = FALSE}
# The reference and the BibTeX entry below are both built from the package's
# own citation (inst/CITATION, which takes the version from the installed
# package), so this page and citation("theoryforge") cannot disagree, and no
# year or version is written by hand here.
cit <- utils::citation("theoryforge")
ver <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("theoryforge"))
```

## Citing theoryforge

If you use the R package in your work, please cite it:

<p style="margin: 0 0 0.6em 0; padding-left: 1.8em; text-indent: -1.8em;">Bernabeu, P. (`r cit$year`). <em>theoryforge: Systematic theory development</em> (R package version `r ver`). Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN). <a href="https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.theoryforge">https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.theoryforge</a></p>

```{r bibtex-entry, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# The entry is citation()'s, with the key theoryforge, which citation() leaves
# empty. It is shown with a copy button and a download link. The button uses
# the browser clipboard API, and the link is a self-contained data URI, so
# neither depends on a static file being shipped alongside the site.
bib <- paste(utils::toBibtex(cit), collapse = "\n")
bib <- sub("@Manual{,", "@Manual{theoryforge,", bib, fixed = TRUE)
esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}
uri <- paste0(
  "data:application/x-bibtex;charset=utf-8,",
  utils::URLencode(bib, reserved = TRUE)
)
cat(sprintf(
'<div class="citation-bibtex">
<pre id="theoryforge-bibtex"><code>%s</code></pre>
<p class="citation-bibtex-actions">
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" onclick="theoryforgeCopyBibtex(this)">Copy BibTeX</button>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm" download="theoryforge.bib" href="%s">Download .bib</a>
</p>
</div>
<script>
function theoryforgeCopyBibtex(btn) {
  var code = document.getElementById("theoryforge-bibtex");
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.innerText).then(function () {
    var label = btn.textContent;
    btn.textContent = "Copied";
    setTimeout(function () { btn.textContent = label; }, 1500);
  });
}
</script>
', esc(bib), uri))
```

In R, `citation("theoryforge")` gives the same entry with its key left empty. The package
installs from CRAN with `install.packages("theoryforge")`, and the development version with
`remotes::install_github("pablobernabeu/theoryforge", subdir = "r/theoryforge")`.

## The developer

theoryforge is developed and maintained by
[Pablo Bernabeu](https://pablobernabeu.github.io), a researcher in the
Department of Education at the University of Oxford. His work spans cognitive psychology and
neuroscience, linguistics, education and digital technologies, and research methods and open
science. He has hands-on experience in behavioural and EEG experiments, corpus analysis,
computational modelling and statistics. He develops open, reproducible research software in R
and Python, and is a Fellow of the Software Sustainability Institute. His
[ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1083-2460) lists his other work.

This R package has a twin written in Python, documented on the
[theoryforge (Python) site](https://pablobernabeu.github.io/theoryforge/python/). Both
implement one
[specification](https://github.com/pablobernabeu/theoryforge/blob/main/API_SPEC.md) and are
tested against the same expected outputs, apart from the functions that call a network service,
an embedding model or a renderer.

## Versions and archiving

CRAN assigned the package the DOI <https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.theoryforge> on
publication. It names the R package across all its versions, so the version in the citation
identifies the release used. Releases of the repository, which also holds the Python twin,
are tagged on [GitHub](https://github.com/pablobernabeu/theoryforge/releases) and archived on
Zenodo, which gives each release a DOI of its own. The concept DOI,
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21229964>, resolves to the latest archived release. The
[changelog](../news/index.html) records what changed in each release.

## Contributing and support

Bugs and feature requests can be reported on the
[GitHub issues page](https://github.com/pablobernabeu/theoryforge/issues), and the
[contributing guide](../CONTRIBUTING.html) explains how to set up a development environment
and propose a change. The OSF deposit adapter takes a personal access token, so never paste
that token, or any other secret, into an issue. Replace it with a placeholder.
